answer.rationale: Timeline is the strongest signal available: a release landed 2h ago and write-path p99 began climbing 90m ago, a lag consistent with a build-induced regression surfacing under load. memory_b1 records a rollback cleanly resolving a checkout error spike, and memory_b6 records that release-linked regressions here have been real and detectable within an hour — so rollback is the intervention whose causal story matches the evidence and which does not trade writes away. I want the archived source for b1 (does it actually establish rollback-as-cause, or only correlation, and was it done under heavy write load?) and b6 (does canary/staging evidence let me confirm this specific build before I move the whole fleet?), because those are the two memories I am leaning on to act, not the ones I am leaning on to abstain. memory_b2 is decisive but self-limiting and needs no verification: it already carries its own caveat, writes are hot right now, and a 40-minute replication gap with lost customer writes directly violates the primary objective — regional_failover is excluded regardless of what the archive says. add_capacity (b3) addressed a forecast surge, not a post-release regression, and would likely mask rather than fix. route_read_replicas (b5) helped when dashboard reads were starving the primary; nothing here points to read contention, and settlement peak is a write phenomenon. enable_circuit_breaker (b4) contained an external partner failure; there is no partner dependency implicated, and failing fast during settlement peak sheds exactly the customer writes I am meant to protect. Residual uncertainty is real: settlement peak alone could be driving this, in which case rollback buys nothing and consumes the only window. That is why I stage rather than sweep — canary cohort first per b6, confirm p99 recovery in that cohort, then progress. Risk to flag downstream: a rollback executed mid-settlement can itself drop in-flight writes if the prior build's schema or write path differs, so drain and verify write-path compatibility before promoting beyond canary; and if the canary does not recover, do not escalate to failover in the next window while writes remain hot.
